title: Mashed Potatoes
description:
From Joel Robuchon, these Parisian potatoes are outrageous – almost equivalent to one stick of butter for every big potato!
Mashed Potatoes Served Three Ways
Bring a big pot of salted water to boil.
Meanwhile, peel and cut potatoes and place in pot of cold water while the pot on the stove is getting to a boil.
Add the potatoes to the boiling water and boil about 10-15 minutes, until soft.
Meanwhile, in a saucepan or microwave, heat butter and milk together until butter melts and the mixture steams.
Drain potatoes well and return to the hot pot. Using a ricer or other tool, mash the hot potatoes until smooth.
ingredients: 2 ½ pounds (about 6 large potatoes, a combination russet (baking) potatoes and Yukon Golds, or all
directions: In the hot pot, lightly mix in about half of the hot butter mixture, just until blended. Taste for salt and add more butter mixture until seasoned to your liking.
Bring a big pot of salted water to boil.
Meanwhile, cut potatoes in half and place in pot of cold water while the pot on the stove is getting to a boil.
Add the potatoes to the boiling water and boil about 10-15 minutes, until soft.
Drain potatoes well and return to the hot pot. Smash potatoes roughly with a masher or a big wooden spoon, leaving some lumps.
Combine with butter, sour cream, and cheese. When cheese melts into the potatoes, add the chives and salt and pepper to taste.
Place potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water up to one inch above the potatoes, and add a couple of big pinches of salt. Cook at a simmer for 30 minutes or until done.
Meanwhile, bring the milk to a boil, and cut the butter up into small pieces (keep chilled).
When done, drain and peel the potatoes while still warm.

Puree the potatoes through a ricer (or food processor) and return to the pot to dry out, stirring with a wooden spoon, for 2-3 minutes. Stir in the butter pieces, then slowly add the hot milk in a fine stream.
Using a whisk, make sure the puree is extremely smooth before serving.

These are also good with a roasted and smashed whole head of garlic or some other special roasted root vegetable, like parsnips. You could also use a little olive oil instead of butter for a more rustic flavor.
You hardly need or want any gravy when you have good, fresh mashed potatoes.
